segments.narration: A New Hampshire mountain grew five feet taller overnight in 1930. State cartographers stared at their transit scopes in absolute disbelief.
Government surveyors re-checked their brass bench markers on the summit ridge. Every measurement confirmed the impossible data.
Local newspapers blamed shifting tectonic faults or hidden underground caverns collapsing. But how does millions of tons of solid stone suddenly shift vertically?
Geologists discovered that massive subsurface frost action can literally shove solid bedrock upward. Water trapped deep inside microscopic rock fractures froze rapidly.
Freezing groundwater expands and ratchets the entire crust upward through cryogenesis. Mother Nature built a hydraulic jack right inside the mountain.
